settings.window_mica_desc: The desktop's colour, softly blurred, under the title bar, tabs and sidebar, as in Windows 11's own apps. Terminals stay solid.

zmodem.pick_folder: Choose where to save (the remote is running sz)

zmodem.send_files_hint: Send files: types rz on the other end and sends what you pick
zmodem.no_rz: rz did not start on the other end. Is lrzsz installed there?
zmodem.download_folder_hint: Download the current folder: runs sz on every file under it, folders kept
zmodem.no_sz: sz did not start on the other end. Is lrzsz installed there?
zmodem.multiplexer: rz/sz cannot pass through tmux or screen, so it was stopped. Use the Send and Download buttons on the terminal bar, which work in tmux tabs, or run it outside tmux.

hostkey.changed_warning: The host key for {{host}} has CHANGED. This could be a man-in-the-middle attack — or the server was reinstalled. Only continue if you trust this change.
terminal.paste_confirm_message: You're about to paste {{lines}} lines. Multi-line text can run as commands the moment it's pasted. Paste anyway?
terminal.paste_dont_ask: Don't ask again — you can turn this back on in Settings

session.open_vnc_bmc_hint: The iDRAC's own VNC server, with the VNC password saved in the session
session.name: Session name
quick_connect.telnet_hint: Typed in when the device asks to log in. To keep other Telnet settings, save it as a session.
session.no_sessions_vault: No sessions in this vault. Create one to get started.
session.key_missing: This session uses an imported key that is not in this vault. Import it here, or switch to a key file.
session.key_forget_confirm: Remove this key from the vault?
session.key_none_imported: No keys imported yet. Import one and it works on every machine you sign in from.
session.key_will_ask: Asks for its passphrase on connect
session.key_import_explain: The key is stored encrypted in your vault, so sessions that use it connect from any machine you sign in from — no copying key files around.
session.key_import_passphrase_hint: Leave empty if the key has none
session.close_active_message: You have {{count}} active connection(s). Closing now will terminate them. Are you sure you want to close?
session.login_shell_hint: Run a specific shell instead of the remote default (e.g. fish -l).
session.key_public_warning: This is a public key. SSH needs the matching private key.
session.key_not_recognized: This file isn't a recognized SSH key.
session.os_cleared: Cleared. The OS is detected again on the next connect.
session.notes_placeholder: Anything worth knowing about this server
session.field_hidden_hint: Masked until you reveal it. Search skips hidden values.
winbox.desktop_only: WinBox runs in the desktop app only.
winbox.editor_hint: Opens in MikroTik's WinBox 4 with this login. Where WinBox is, and how the password reaches it, are set in Settings > Sessions.
winbox.started_copied: WinBox started for {{name}}. The password is on the clipboard for 45 seconds: paste it into WinBox.
settings.winbox_path_desc: The WinBox 4 program WinBox sessions open in. Empty: found by itself.
settings.winbox_not_found: WinBox 4 was not found. Get it from mikrotik.com/download/winbox, or pick the program.
settings.winbox_path_bad: Nothing usable at this path. Pick the WinBox program (WinBox.exe, WinBox, or WinBox.app on a Mac).
settings.winbox_password_desc: How a saved password reaches WinBox. On the command line WinBox logs in by itself, but other programs on this computer can read it while WinBox runs. On the clipboard it stays 45 seconds, for you to paste.
session.telnet_login_hint: Telnet has no login of its own. Reach types the username and password in when the device asks for them (a Username:, login: or Password: prompt) in the first minute.
session.telnet_mode_hint: Raw TCP is for the serial ports of a console server. If a device misbehaves when Reach starts the Telnet negotiation, let the device start.
session.term_type_hint: What the server is told this terminal is (TERM). Old devices may want vt100. Used from the next connect.
session.term_type_invalid: The terminal type must be one word of plain letters, digits and symbols, at most 64 characters.
session.encoding_hint: The character set the server speaks. Pick ISO-8859-2 or windows-1250 for an old device that shows Czech letters wrong.
session.telnet_keys_hint: Change these only if lines come out doubled or Backspace shows ^H or ^? on the device.
session.wsl_windows_only: WSL is only available on Windows
session.x11_desktop_only: X11 desktops open in the desktop app only.
session.wsl_user_hint: Leave empty to sign in as the default user. wsl.exe signs in by itself, so there is no password to keep.
session.vnc_password_hint: The server's VNC password, if it has one. VNC uses only the first 8 characters.
session.vnc_mac_username_placeholder: Leave empty for a VNC password
session.vnc_mac_username_hint: For a Mac (Screen Sharing or Apple Remote Desktop): the macOS account to log in as. Leave empty for a server with a VNC password.
session.vnc_mac_password_hint: The macOS account's password. It never leaves this computer: the Mac checks it with SRP. Macs that offer only the older Apple login are reached through an SSH session.
session.vnc_via_hint: VNC itself is not encrypted. Through a saved SSH session it is, and the VNC port can stay closed to the network; the host above is then as that SSH server sees it, such as localhost.
session.vnc_encryption_hint: VeNCrypt is the encryption QEMU/libvirt, TigerVNC and wayvnc offer; the server needs an X.509 certificate. TLS for the whole connection is for servers with SSL encryption, such as an iDRAC. A certificate this computer does not trust is shown on the first connect, to trust it for this session.
session.vnc_encryption_none_hint: Without encryption, VNC is readable on the network; connect through an SSH session below, or choose VeNCrypt if the server has it.
session.vnc_vencrypt_username_hint: Only for a server that logs in with a user name and password (VeNCrypt X509Plain, as wayvnc). Leave empty for a VNC password.
session.vnc_vencrypt_password_hint: The password for that user name. It is sent inside TLS.
session.rdp_password_hint: Stored encrypted in vault. Leave empty to be asked on connect.
session.rdp_share_hint: Shown inside the remote desktop as a drive. Not available on Android.
session.rdp_share_all_drives_hint: Windows: every drive letter. macOS and Linux: your home folder, the root and mounted disks. The remote can then read and change all of them.
session.rdp_files_port_hint: Open file manager in the session menu reaches this machine over SFTP on this port, with the same login. Windows needs OpenSSH Server turned on. Empty: 22.
session.rdp_files_hint: This machine's files over SFTP, with the same login
session.rdp_sftp_help_title: Turn on SFTP on the server
session.rdp_sftp_help_intro: Nothing answered on {{host}}:{{port}}. The file manager connects over SFTP, so the server needs an SSH server. Windows has one, OpenSSH Server, but it is off by default:
session.rdp_sftp_help_2025: Windows Server 2025: already installed. Turn on Remote SSH Access in Server Manager, or start the sshd service.
session.rdp_sftp_help_2019: Windows Server 2019 and 2022 (and Windows 10 and 11): add OpenSSH Server under Settings > Apps > Optional features, or run this in PowerShell as administrator:
session.rdp_sftp_help_old: Windows Server 2016 and older: nothing built in. Install Microsoft's Win32-OpenSSH from GitHub, or another SFTP server such as Bitvise.
session.rdp_sftp_help_after: SFTP works as soon as sshd runs, and setup opens port 22 in the firewall. Log in as for RDP (user or DOMAIN\user). A different port can be set in the session's RDP settings (File manager SSH port). On Linux, install and start openssh-server.
session.rdp_share_app_files: Share this app's folder in Files
session.rdp_share_app_files_hint: The "Shared with desktops" folder, under this app in the Files app, shows inside the remote desktop as a drive.
session.rdp_client_freerdp_hint: Uses the FreeRDP 3 client configured in Settings › Remote desktop.
session.rdp_clipboard_hint: What copy and paste carries between this computer and the desktop.
session.rdp_forward_lock_keys_hint: Send Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock presses to the remote desktop for shortcuts. The lock states stay synced either way.
session.rdp_resolution_hint: A fixed size is scaled to fit the window.
session.rdp_keyboard_hint: The layout the remote session starts with.
session.rdp_performance_fast: Fastest: no wallpaper, themes or animations
session.rdp_keepalive_hint: Sends a little input while idle, so firewalls do not drop the connection.
session.rdp_jiggler_hint: Moves the mouse slightly while you are away, so the remote does not lock or go idle.
session.rdp_program: Start a program instead of the desktop
session.rdp_program_hint: Leave empty for the full desktop. The session ends when the program closes.
session.rdp_remote_app_hint: Shows just the program's windows, no remote desktop, with a button for each window above them. Use ||name for an app published on the server. The server must allow RemoteApp.
session.rdp_app_program_missing: A RemoteApp needs a program to run.
session.rdp_app_windows_separate_hint: The program's windows appear on your desktop like local ones. The remote desktop takes the size of this screen. Moving a window is done by the remote side, so it follows with a short delay. On Wayland the windows may not land where they should.
session.rdp_auth_kerberos_hint: Gets a Kerberos ticket from the domain with the login above, falling back to NTLM when no KDC answers. Connect to the server by its full DNS name, not an IP address, and log in as user@domain or with the domain's DNS name.
session.rdp_kdc_hint: A domain controller (host or host:port), or a KDC proxy URL such as https://gateway.example.com/KdcProxy. Empty: found in DNS or the system's Kerberos settings.
session.rdp_gateway_hint: Connect through a Remote Desktop Gateway: its name, with :port when not 443. The server above is then reached by the gateway, by its name on the inside network.
session.rdp_gateway_rpc: RPC over HTTP (gateways before Windows Server 2012)
session.rdp_gateway_own_login: The gateway has its own login
session.rdp_gateway_same_login: The gateway gets this session's login (with its domain).
rdp.remote_app_separate: The program runs in windows of its own
rdp.remote_app_separate_hint: Use the buttons above to bring a window back. Closing this tab ends the session and closes them.
session.fallback_to_password: Key was rejected by the server. Enter your password to try again.
session.identity_created_toast: Identity created. Your encryption key is stored securely in the OS keychain.
session.data_cleared_toast: Data cleared. You can now initialize.
session.secure_sessions_desc: Your sessions are encrypted locally. Click to generate your encryption key (stored securely in OS keychain).
session.keychain_error_desc: Your encrypted data exists but the OS keychain key is missing. Import your backup key to recover, or start fresh (data will be lost).
session.link_device_hint: Already syncing on another device? Paste its link code to open the same vaults.
session.keychain_locked_desc: Unable to access keychain. Please check OS permissions.
session.share_hint: The recipient can now accept this share using your vault's sync URL.
session.recipient_required: Recipient UUID and public key are required
session.invalid_public_key_length: Invalid public key: must be 32 bytes (X25519)
session.invalid_public_key_base64: Invalid public key: must be valid base64
tunnel.no_ssh_sessions: Save an SSH session first to create a tunnel.
tunnel.no_tunnels: No tunnels configured. Create one to get started.

explorer.columns_hint: Click to sort, right-click to choose columns
explorer.terminal_folder_unknown: This server does not say which folder the terminal is in (Linux servers do)
explorer.drop_no_files: No files detected. Drag files from your file manager.

vault.import_backup_desc: Restore your Reach data from an encrypted backup file.

vault.delete_vault_warning: This will permanently delete this vault and all its secrets. This action cannot be undone.
vault.type_private_hint: Only you can access this vault.
vault.type_shared_hint: Team members can be invited to access this vault.
vault.invite_created_msg: Invite created! Share this info with the invitee:
vault.delete_vault_confirm: Are you sure you want to delete this vault? This will permanently delete all secrets in this vault.
vault.password_min_chars: Password must be at least 8 characters

vault.duplicate_hint: Merging keeps one entry on this device. All connections stay: they are stored in the vault itself, and nothing changes for anyone else.
settings.title: Settings
settings.x11_desc: Shows windows of programs you start on a server (X11 forwarding). Turning it on downloads VcXsrv, about 49 MB, once.
settings.x11_installed: VcXsrv {{version}} is ready. Sessions with ForwardX11 show their windows here. Turn off to remove it.
settings.x11_system: This system's own X server is used for X11 forwarding.
settings.x11_mac: X11 forwarding on a Mac needs XQuartz (xquartz.org).
settings.x11_failed: The X11 server could not be set up: {{error}}
themes.pair_hint: Follows your computer: the light theme below while it is in light mode, the dark one while it is in dark mode.
themes.pair_now_dark: Your system is dark right now.
themes.pair_now_light: Your system is light right now.
themes.error: Could not reach the theme registry
settings.paste_warning_desc: A pasted newline runs the command as soon as it arrives. Ask first, so a stray copy cannot execute on a server before you have read it.
settings.paste_threshold_desc: Pastes with fewer lines than this go straight to the terminal.
settings.term_right_click_desc: Open a menu with Copy and Paste, or act at once. Ctrl+right click always opens the menu. A program that uses the mouse (mc, vim) gets the click; hold Shift to keep it.
settings.term_copy_on_select_desc: Text selected in the terminal goes to the clipboard at once.
settings.term_middle_click_desc: On Linux it pastes the selected text, elsewhere the clipboard.
settings.term_word_separators_desc: A double click selects up to a space or one of these characters. Remove one to keep it inside the word; add : or / to stop there.
settings.double_click_open: Open sessions with a double click
settings.double_click_open_desc: A single click picks a session in the list; a double click connects. Enter still connects.
settings.show_unsupported_sessions: Show sessions this device can't open
settings.show_unsupported_sessions_desc: Sessions this device can't open, such as WinBox or serial ones on a phone, stay in the list greyed out. Tapping one says why; you can still edit it. Off: they are hidden.
settings.close_tab_on_exit: Close the tab when a session ends
settings.close_tab_on_exit_desc: When the shell ends on its own (you type exit), its tab closes instead of offering Reconnect. So does an RDP desktop you log off from. A dropped connection still offers it.
settings.reopen_windows_desc: Session windows open when the app closed open again where they were, with their saved sessions and local shells. Quick Connect tabs are not reopened.
settings.rerun_setup_desc: Go through the first-run questions again: theme, sessions, copy and paste, logs and history, security and updates.
settings.server_monitoring_desc: Show CPU, memory, disk and logged-in users of the server under SSH and WSL terminals. A session can turn it on or off for itself in its settings.
settings.check_updates_desc: Look for a new release when Reach starts and every 45 minutes. Turned off, nothing is fetched unless you press Check now.
settings.shell_colors: Type a colour setup into the shell
settings.shell_colors_desc: Off by default. Servers colour their own prompt and ls for Reach's xterm-256color terminal, as they do for PuTTY. When on, Reach types a short colour and prompt setup after login; it keeps it out of bash and zsh history, but a few shells (BusyBox, some zsh setups) may still record it.
settings.more_fonts: More fonts: {{count}}. Search to narrow the list.
settings.fonts_hidden: Proportional fonts that match: {{count}}. Turn on Show all fonts to list them.
settings.rdp_hw_render_desc: Paint the desktop through the GPU. Applies to desktops opened after the change.
settings.rdp_gfx_desc: Ask the host for the graphics pipeline, which carries video as H.264 on hosts that encode it. On a host that does not, the picture gets heavier, not lighter.
settings.rdp_gfx_new_desc: Let the graphics pipeline use AVC444 (sharper text and colour in H.264) and RemoteFX progressive (GNOME Remote Desktop uses it). Turn off if a host shows a broken picture or drops the session; the older formats are then used.
settings.freerdp_path_desc: Choose the executable for FreeRDP sessions. Leave blank to detect an installed FreeRDP 3 client.
settings.freerdp_path_bad: The selected executable could not be found or run.
settings.freerdp_not_found: FreeRDP was not detected. Install FreeRDP 3 or browse to its executable.
settings.rdp_fs_button_desc: Show the Full screen button over a remote desktop. Drag it anywhere to keep it clear of the remote's own buttons; it stays where you put it. Without it, Ctrl+Alt+Enter still toggles full screen.
settings.rdp_bar_pinned_desc: Pin the bar at the top of a full-screen remote desktop so it stays shown; otherwise it hides and comes back when the mouse touches the top edge. The pin on the bar itself does the same.
settings.shell_desc: Shell used when opening new local terminals.
settings.restore_tabs_desc: Open the tabs you had when Reach last closed.
settings.tray_desc: Keep running in system tray when window is closed.
settings.community_desc: Chat, support and release announcements on Discord.
settings.website_desc: Reach's home page: downloads, install steps and features.
settings.license_desc: Reacher CM is free software under the MIT License.
report.title: Report a problem
report.desc: Opens a GitHub issue with Reach's log to attach, cleaned of your hosts, accounts and folders.
report.cleaned: This is the log as it will be shared. Your hosts, user names, session names, IP addresses and home folder were replaced. Read it, and remove anything else you would rather keep private.
report.partial: Saved sessions could not be read, so their hosts and names may still be in this log. Read it before you attach it.
report.after: The issue is open in your browser. Describe what happened, then drag reach-report.log from the folder that just opened into the issue.
settings.support_desc: Reach is free and built on no budget. Sponsoring is what would pay for a signing certificate, a test server, and the time to build more.

community.body: There is a Discord for Reach. Ask questions, hear about new versions, or help decide where it goes next.

community.point_releases: New versions announced as they ship
settings.system_startup_desc: Launch Reach automatically when you log in.
settings.play_sounds_desc: A short chime when a notification appears, and the terminal bell's sound. Off by default on phones and tablets.
settings.toast_position_desc: Where notifications appear in the window.
settings.notification_history_desc: Keep the last day's notifications behind the bell in the top bar, on this device only.
settings.system_notifications_desc: Show notifications as system notifications too: while the app is in the background, or always instead of in the app. Notifications with a button still show in the app.
notifications.history_empty: No notifications in the last day.
notifications.history_kept: Kept for one day, on this device only.
settings.bell_sound_desc: A short ping when a program rings the terminal bell (^G). Silent while Play sounds is off. On by default on desktop.
settings.bell_flash_desc: The terminal's edge lights up briefly when the bell rings. On by default on phones and tablets.
settings.bell_notify_desc: A system notification when the bell rings in a tab you are not looking at, or while the app is in the background. At most one every 10 seconds per tab.
settings.bell_notify_denied: Notifications are not allowed for Reacher CM. Allow them in the system settings, then turn this on again.
settings.font_desc: Font used in the terminal emulator.
security.password_too_short: Password must be at least 8 characters
sync.backup_key_warning: Store this key securely. You will need it to restore your identity if you lose access to your OS keychain.
sync.cloud_sync_desc: Your personal data in a Turso database of your own, and shared vaults that others invite you to.
sync.accept_invite_desc: Enter the sync URL and token from the vault owner to join their shared vault.
sync.link_device_desc: Each device makes its own encryption identity, and a vault made by one cannot be opened by another. Show a link code here and paste it on the other device to open the same vaults there.
sync.link_code_warning: Anyone with this code can open your vaults. Move it to your other device yourself, over a channel you trust, and do not keep it anywhere.
sync.join_device_desc: Paste the link code from a device that already syncs. This device then opens the same vaults instead of its own.
sync.join_confirm: This device's own identity and the data in it are replaced by the other device's. Click again to continue.
sync.joined_toast: Joined. This device now opens the same vaults.
sync.personal_db_exists: This Turso organization already holds a personal vault from another device ({{names}}). It can only be opened with that device's identity: on that device open Settings > Sync > Link another device, then paste the code here under Join from another device. Click Save again to create a separate vault anyway.
sync.link_qr_hint: On the other device, tap Scan QR code (on its first screen or under Join from another device), or paste the code below.
sync.cloud_sync_enabled: Cloud sync enabled for all data
sync.url_token_required: Both sync URL and token are required
sync.cloud_sync_active: Your personal data syncs to this database.
backup.export_desc: Create an encrypted backup of all your vaults, secrets, and settings.
backup.import_desc: Restore your data from an encrypted backup file.
backup.import_warning: Importing will replace your current data. This cannot be undone.
backup.password_too_short: Password must be at least 8 characters

ai_settings.unlock_vault: Unlock vault to enter API key securely
ai_settings.no_models: No models loaded. Validate your API key to load available models.

setup.paste_warning_hint: Asks before a paste of several lines reaches the shell.
setup.logging_subtitle: Both are off unless you turn them on
setup.log_hint: Saves what the server prints to a text file, as PuTTY does.
setup.history_hint: An encrypted record you can search with Ctrl+Shift+H. Passwords you type are never saved.
setup.logging_per_session: Each session can choose otherwise in its own settings.

setup.unlock_keys_hint: Ask once at start for your keys' passphrases; kept in memory only.
setup.check_updates_hint: Look for a new release at start and every 45 minutes. Off: only Check now in Settings > About does.

toolchain.python_required: Python 3 is required to install Ansible
sharing.title: Session sharing
sharing.start_desc: You make a code and send it to them.
sharing.join_desc: You paste the code they sent you.
sharing.read_write_warn: They will be able to type into your terminal as you. Enforced on this machine; you can switch it back at any time.
sharing.preparing: Finding a route… this takes a few seconds.
sharing.waiting: Waiting for them to connect. Send them this reply now: it works for a couple of minutes. This closes on its own once they connect.
sharing.fail_no_path: No route between the two machines. This is almost always a NAT that blocks direct connections. It works if both of you are on the same network or VPN, or with a TURN server added under Settings → Sharing.
sharing.fail_bad_code: That code is not for this share. Check it was copied completely.
sharing.fail_tampered: A message arrived that could not be verified, so the connection was closed.
sharing.fail_timeout: The other side did not connect in time.

security.unlock_keys_at_start_desc: When Reach opens, ask once for the passphrase of each passphrase-protected key your saved credentials use. The passphrases are kept in memory only, until Reach locks or closes, so connecting does not ask again, also with a session that picks the same key itself. Keys only sessions use are not asked for here; a passphrase typed for one at a connect is kept the same way.
security.keys_biometric_desc: A passphrase typed when keys are unlocked at start is kept on this device behind {{method}}, so the next start asks for {{method}} once instead of each passphrase. The passphrases never go into the vault and do not sync. Enrolling a new face or fingerprint voids them; you type them once more.
security.keys_windows_hello_desc: Keep passphrases typed during startup on this device. The next vault unlock asks for Windows Hello once for all remembered keys. Windows may offer your Hello PIN.

help.docker_permission_body: Docker's socket belongs to root and the docker group, and your SSH user is in neither. Rootless Docker runs it as your own user; adding yourself to the docker group works too, but read the warning first.
help.docker_rootless: Safest: rootless Docker, as your user
help.docker_group: Or add your user to the docker group (then log in again)
help.docker_group_warning: Anyone in the docker group can become root on this server (Docker's own documentation says so).
help.podman_socket_body: Reach talks to Podman through its API socket, which is started by systemd for your user. Start it once and it stays on.

help.engine_missing_body: The command wasn't found. Install Docker or Podman on the server, or choose the other engine in the host's settings.
help.read_only_body: Changes are refused here. To make changes, turn Read-only off in its settings.
help.k8s_unauthorized_title: The cluster didn't accept your credentials
help.k8s_unauthorized_body: The kubeconfig's token or certificate was refused, often because it expired. Get a fresh kubeconfig and edit the cluster to replace it.
help.k8s_forbidden_title: Your account isn't allowed to do that
help.k8s_forbidden_body: The cluster's RBAC rules don't give this identity that permission. Ask the cluster's administrator, or use an account that has it.

k8s.hint_crash: The container starts and then exits, again and again. The Logs tab usually says why.
k8s.hint_evicted: The node ran short of memory or disk and removed this pod. Its controller usually starts a replacement elsewhere.
k8s.hint_image: The image cannot be downloaded. Check the image name and tag, and that the cluster may pull from that registry.
k8s.hint_oom: The container used more memory than its limit and was stopped. Raise the limit or find what uses the memory.

k8s.kc_cloud: Their command-line tools write it to ~/.kube/config:
k8s.kubeconfig_hint: Paste or choose a kubeconfig. It is stored encrypted in your vault. Reach asks before running a credential helper or sharing the selected context’s credentials with remote Helm.
k8s.kubeconfig_keep: Leave empty to keep the stored kubeconfig
k8s.kubeconfig_keep_hint: The stored kubeconfig is kept unless you paste or choose a new one.
k8s.kubeconfig_too_big: That file is too large to be a kubeconfig.

sshopt.title: SSH options (ssh_config)
sshalg.title: SSH algorithms
sshalg.hint_default: Modern algorithms only, as current OpenSSH offers. Very old devices may refuse to connect.
sshalg.hint_compatible: Also offers the SHA-1 key exchange, CBC ciphers, SHA-1 and MD5 MACs and ssh-rsa key logins that old switches, routers and appliances need. Weaker, so use it only for devices that cannot do better.
sshalg.hint_custom: Pick each algorithm yourself. Those marked legacy weaken the connection.
sshalg.pubkey_sha1: Allow ssh-rsa (SHA-1) signatures for key login
sshalg.forward_agent_hint: Lets the server use your local agent's keys while you are connected. Use it only with servers you trust.
sshalg.forward_x11_hint: Lets programs on the server open windows on this computer.
sshopt.intro: Settings as you would write them in ~/.ssh/config. Reach applies them to this session, on every device it syncs to.
sshopt.lines_hint: Any ssh_config keyword, e.g. MACs +hmac-sha1. Lines written here win over an imported file, as ssh -o does.
sshopt.reread_missing: There is no Host {{alias}} in ~/.ssh/config any more.
sshopt.approval_hint: These make the connection weaker than Reach's defaults, or run a program on this computer. Nothing here is used until you tick it.
sshopt.not_yet: Kept with the session, not acted on yet
sshopt.session_field: Used as the session's own setting
sshopt.structure: Shapes how the file is read
sshopt.status_overridden: An earlier line already set this
sshopt.other_host_lines: Lines for other hosts, not shown: {{count}}
sshopt.status_inactive: In a block that does not apply to this host
sshopt.status_deprecated: No longer does anything in OpenSSH
sshopt.status_unsupported: OpenSSH itself no longer supports this
sshopt.import_desc: Each host is read the way ssh reads it, with Match, Include and every option. The files are kept with the session, so it connects the same way on every device.
sshopt.file_errors_title: ssh would refuse your config because of these lines:
sshopt.weaker_hint: You allowed these. Untick one to stop using it.
authprompt.title_confirm: Add the key to the SSH agent?
authprompt.host_hint: Asked while logging in to {{host}}. Nothing you type here is saved.
authprompt.unlock_detail: Enter the passphrase for the key '{{key}}', used by: {{credentials}}.
authprompt.unlock_retry: That passphrase does not open this key. Try again.
authprompt.unlock_hint: Kept in memory until Reach locks or closes; nothing is saved. Cancel to be asked when you connect.
hostkey.dns_match: Matching host key fingerprint found in DNS.
hostkey.dns_nomatch: No matching host key fingerprint found in DNS.
hostkey.save_to_session: Accept and save keeps this key with the session, so it syncs with it. Accept once connects without keeping it.
hostkey.save_to_device: Accept and save keeps this key on this device. Accept once connects without keeping it.
hostkeys.title: Trusted host keys
hostkeys.hint: The server keys this session trusts, kept with the session so they sync with it. Jump hosts have their own.
hostkeys.empty: No host key saved yet. Choose Accept and save the next time you connect.
hostkeys.replace_hint: Paste the fingerprint as ssh-keygen -lf prints it on the server (SHA256:…). The next connect accepts only this key.
security.host_keys_remove_all_desc: Remove every server key saved on your sessions and on this device. Each server is asked about again on its next connect.
security.host_keys_remove_all_confirm: Remove all saved host keys? Sessions in shared vaults lose theirs for everyone in the vault.
security.host_keys_removed: Removed from {{sessions}} sessions and {{device}} servers on this device.
security.host_keys_remove_failed: {{count}} sessions could not be changed (their vault does not allow it).
ssh.weak_kex: {{host}} is not using a post-quantum key exchange ({{kex}}): the session could be recorded now and decrypted later. Upgrading the server fixes it.
pwmanager.intro: Point a session's password or passphrase at an entry in a password manager instead of saving it in Reach. Passbolt, 1Password and Bitwarden are supported through their command-line tools, and KeePass databases are read directly.
pwmanager.enable_desc: Let saved sessions and database connections take a password from a password manager.
pwmanager.cli_missing: Not found. Install it, or set its path below.
pwmanager.not_configured: Not set up yet: fill in the details below and save.
pwmanager.install_hint: Install go-passbolt-cli (version 0.4 or later). With Homebrew:
pwmanager.install_release: Or download a release (zip, deb, rpm) from GitHub and put passbolt on your PATH.
pwmanager.cli_path_hint: Leave empty to use passbolt from PATH.
pwmanager.credentials_reach_desc: Reach keeps the server address, your private key and its passphrase, encrypted in the vault.
pwmanager.credentials_cli_desc: Use the configuration go-passbolt-cli already has on this computer (made with passbolt configure).
pwmanager.server_https: The address must start with https://
pwmanager.private_key_hint: Your Passbolt account's OpenPGP private key, armored (from the recovery kit). It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
pwmanager.private_key_selected: {{name}} will be read when you save
pwmanager.passphrase_replace: New passphrase (empty keeps the saved one)
pwmanager.totp_secret_replace: New TOTP secret (empty keeps the saved one)
pwmanager.totp_hint: The base32 secret behind your authenticator's QR code. Reach generates the codes when it signs in.
pwmanager.timeout_hint: How long one sign-in and fetch may take: {{min}} to {{max}} seconds.
pwmanager.test_needs_enable: Turn on password managers to test.
pwmanager.note: Secrets are fetched from the password manager when you connect; they are never stored in sessions or shown here. Every fetch is a full Passbolt sign-in, so connecting takes a moment longer.
pwmanager.ref_clear: Stop using the password manager for {{name}}
pwmanager.ref_unavailable: This password manager is turned off or not set up; connecting will fail until it is.
pwmanager.search_placeholder: Search by name, user or address
pwmanager.list_capped: Showing the first {{count}}. Search to narrow it down.
pwmanager.picker_hint: Only names and addresses are listed here. The password is fetched when you connect.
pwmanager.prompt_uses_ref: The secret comes from {{name}}. Type one here to use it for this attempt instead.
pwmanager.cli_path_device: Kept on this device only, not synced. It must be the passbolt program itself (a file named passbolt or passbolt.exe) on this computer.
pwmanager.totp_warning: The TOTP secret is stored next to the private key and passphrase in your vault, and syncs with it. On this device it is not a second factor: whoever can open your vault can sign in to Passbolt as you.
pwmanager.ref_unconfirmed: Not confirmed by you for this session: someone else may have set it. You will be asked before it is used.
pwmanager.untrusted_line: '{{session}}' wants to send your {{provider}} entry '{{entry}}' to {{target}}.
pwmanager.untrusted_line_passphrase: '{{session}}' wants to use your {{provider}} entry '{{entry}}' to unlock the key for {{target}}.
pwmanager.untrusted_warning: Only allow this if you trust whoever last edited this session.
pwmanager.untrusted_reopen: This session's password manager entries are not confirmed for you yet. Connect to it from the session list to confirm them.
pwmanager.untrusted_via_session: It goes through the SSH session '{{name}}': {{route}}.
pwmanager.untrusted_route_lines: ssh_config settings of '{{session}}' that change where it connects:

db.route_lines: Its own ssh_config lines change where it goes:
db.route_unconfirmed: The session this connection goes through has changed since the editor showed it. Check where it goes now and try again.
session.manager_pick_entry: Choose an entry from the password manager, or pick another login method.
pwmanager.reason_error: The password manager could not be checked: {{error}}
pwmanager.reason_none: No password manager is available on this device.
pwmanager.reason_off: Password managers are turned off. Turn them on in Settings → Password managers.
pwmanager.reason_missing: {{name}}: the CLI was not found. Install it or set its path in Settings → Password managers.
pwmanager.reason_unconfigured: {{name}} is not set up yet. Finish it in Settings → Password managers.
pwmanager.passphrase_mode_ask_desc: Reach asks for the passphrase when it signs in to Passbolt and never saves it. While it is remembered, it is held encrypted in memory and handed only to the Passbolt CLI.
pwmanager.passphrase_mode_stored_desc: The passphrase is saved, encrypted, in Reach's vault and used without asking.
pwmanager.credentials_reach_desc_ask: Reach keeps the server address and your private key, encrypted in the vault. The passphrase is asked for when needed.
pwmanager.passphrase_in_memory: A passphrase is remembered right now.
pwmanager.passphrase_not_in_memory: No passphrase is remembered right now.
pwmanager.prompt_retry: That passphrase was not accepted. Try again.
pwmanager.prompt_not_kept: Not kept: Reach will ask again next time.
pwmanager.op_enable_desc: Pick entries from 1Password through its command-line tool, op.
pwmanager.op_install_other: On Linux or Windows, follow 1Password's install guide.
pwmanager.op_cli_path_hint: Leave empty to use op from PATH. Kept on this device only. It must be the op program itself (a file named op or op.exe).
pwmanager.op_auth_app_desc: The 1Password app asks you to approve access (Touch ID, Windows Hello or your password); Reach stores nothing. In the app, turn on Settings → Developer → Integrate with 1Password CLI.
pwmanager.op_auth_service_desc: A service account token saved in Reach's vault. It sees only the vaults shared with the service account, never your Private vault.
pwmanager.op_account_hint: Only needed when the 1Password app is signed in to more than one account: its sign-in address (such as my.1password.com), shorthand or ID.
pwmanager.op_note: The password is read from 1Password each time you connect and is never stored in Reach.
pwmanager.bw_enable_desc: Pick entries from Bitwarden or Vaultwarden through Bitwarden's command-line tool, bw.
pwmanager.bw_install_hint: Install the Bitwarden CLI. With Homebrew:
pwmanager.bw_install_other: Or with npm (npm install -g @bitwarden/cli), or download it from Bitwarden.
pwmanager.bw_cli_path_hint: Leave empty to use bw from PATH. Kept on this device only. It must be the bw program itself (a file named bw or bw.exe).
pwmanager.bw_login_hint: Sign in once in a terminal with bw login (for a self-hosted server, run bw config server with its address first). Reach only unlocks the vault: it asks for your master password when needed and never saves it.
pwmanager.bw_password_in_memory: The master password is remembered right now.
pwmanager.bw_password_not_in_memory: No master password is remembered right now.
pwmanager.bw_note: The password is read from Bitwarden each time you connect and is never stored in Reach. Reach syncs the Bitwarden CLI first, so connecting takes a moment longer.
pwmanager.kp_enable_desc: Pick entries from a KeePass database (.kdbx), as used by KeePass, KeePassXC and others. No extra program is needed.
pwmanager.kp_database_hint: The .kdbx file on this computer. Kept on this device only, not synced. Reach only reads it and never changes it.
pwmanager.kp_key_file_hint: Only if the database is protected with a key file as well as the master password.
pwmanager.kp_note: Reach asks for the database's master password when it needs it and never saves it. The password is read from the file each time you connect and is never stored in Reach.
pwmanager.prompt_retry_master: That master password was not accepted. Try again.
pwmanager.unlock_first: Reach is locked. Unlock Reach first to see or change these settings.

credential.personal_hint: Everyone who uses this vault signs in with their own login, kept in their own vault and never shared: one of their saved credentials, or their default SSH key. They pick it on their first connect.
credential.personal_yours: You sign in with: {{name}}. Change it from the session's menu (My login).
credential.personal_yours_none: You have not picked your login yet. You will be asked on your first connect.
credential.personal_username: User name (used with each person's default key)
credential.personal_pick_desc: "{{name}}" asks everyone to sign in with their own login. Pick yours. It is kept in your own vault, never in the shared one.
credential.personal_default_key_as: As {{username}}, with the key picked in Settings > Security
credential.personal_default_key_desc: With the session's user name and the key picked in Settings > Security
credential.personal_pick_none: Credentials you save in My sessions are listed here too. Add one in the Credentials tab.
credential.personal_menu_hint: Choose which of your own logins you use here
session.key_default_hint: Whoever connects signs in with their own default key, picked in Settings > Security. Use it in a shared vault, so each person uses their own key.
session.key_default_none: You have not picked a default key yet (Settings > Security).
security.default_key_desc: The imported key you sign in with where a session uses "My default key", such as sessions in a shared vault. It stays yours: others use their own.
credential.login_hint: Signs in as {{username}} with the saved credential. Change it in the Credentials tab.
credential.missing_hint: The saved credential is not in this vault (deleted, or not synced yet), so the session's own login is used.
credential.chip_folder: Logs in with {{name}}, from its folder
credential.intro: Logins kept once and used by many sessions in the same vault.
credential.name: Name
credential.edit_hint: Sessions using it now: {{count}}. A change applies to all of them.
credential.vault_hint: Saved in the vault selected above. Only sessions and folders in that vault can use it.
credential.entry_hint: The secret is fetched from your password manager when connecting. Each session using this credential asks once before it uses the entry.
credential.delete_used: Sessions using it: {{sessions}}, folders: {{folders}}. They go back to their own stored login.
credential.delete_unused: No session or folder uses it.
credential.folder_delete_note: {{credentials}} credentials and {{folders}} subfolders move up to {{parent}}.
session.rdm_import_credentials: Save the {{count}} logins from the export as credentials, for {{hosts}} selected hosts
session.rdm_import_credentials_hint: RDM's passwords are not imported: type each one once in the Credentials tab and every session using it gets it. A login a group passes down becomes that folder's credential.
session.mgr_import_desc_mremoteng: Choose the connection file of mRemoteNG or mRemote (confCons.xml, or an XML export), or paste it below. RDP, SSH, Telnet and VNC connections are added as sessions in the selected vault, in folders matching their mRemoteNG folders, with their passwords.
session.mgr_import_desc_mobaxterm: Choose a MobaXterm sessions export (.mxtsessions) or MobaXterm.ini, or paste it below. SSH, Telnet, RDP and VNC sessions are added in folders matching MobaXterm's, with their SSH gateways. Saved passwords come from MobaXterm.ini or this computer's settings; you are asked for MobaXterm's master password.
session.mgr_import_desc_putty: Choose a .reg export of PuTTY's sessions (reg export HKCU\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions putty.reg), or read them from this computer. SSH, Telnet and Raw sessions are added with their key files and SSH proxies; PuTTY does not save passwords.
session.mgr_import_desc_winscp: Choose WinSCP.ini or a .reg export of WinSCP's settings, or read them from this computer. SFTP and SCP sites are added as SSH sessions, in folders matching WinSCP's, with their tunnels and passwords (not when WinSCP has a master password).
session.mgr_import_desc_tabby: Choose Tabby's config.yaml, or read it from this computer. SSH and Telnet profiles are added in folders matching Tabby's groups, with their jump hosts; with Tabby's vault on, its passwords come too, and you are asked for the vault passphrase.
session.mgr_import_not_found: No {{app}} settings were found on this computer.
session.mgr_import_password_hint: The passwords in this file are encrypted. Enter the master password to import them, or import without them; you are then asked for them on connect.
session.mgr_import_password_wrong: That password does not open this file.
session.mgr_import_password_required: This file cannot be read without its password.
session.mgr_import_passwords_skipped: Some passwords could not be read and were left out; you are asked for them on connect.
session.mgr_import_passwords_keychain: Without its vault, Tabby keeps passwords in the system keychain, so none are imported; you are asked for them on connect.
session.mgr_import_encrypted: This file is encrypted in a way that cannot be read here. Save it again without encryption, then import it.
session.mgr_import_none: No SSH, RDP, VNC or Telnet sessions found in that file.
session.mgr_import_user_hint: Some hosts have no username in the file. Enter the username to use for them; to use different ones, filter and import in batches.
session.mgr_import_credentials: Save the {{count}} logins from the file as credentials, for {{hosts}} selected hosts
session.mgr_import_credentials_hint: Each is saved once, with its password when the file has it; a login a folder passes down becomes that folder's credential.

broadcast.palette_remove: Take this tab out of the broadcast

sync.status_desc: Every vault is kept on this device and works offline. Changes go to the backend whenever it can be reached.
sync.status_unavailable: Could not load vault sync status.
sync.conflicts: Conflict copies made: {{count}}. Look for “(conflict copy” in their names.
sync.legacy_format: Old format: Turso can read session names and categories.
sync.upgrade_confirm: After the upgrade Turso stores only sealed records. Reach versions older than this one, on any device, will no longer see this vault's changes, so update Reach everywhere first. The old table is kept as a backup.
sync.upgraded_toast: Vault moved to the sealed format
sync.backend_desc: Where your personal data (sessions, credentials, settings) syncs: your Reacher CM account, a folder, an SMB share, an SFTP server, a Git repository, an S3 bucket or Turso. It is encrypted on this device before it leaves, names included.
sync.kind_folder: Folder (this disk, a network share or a UNC path)
sync.folder_hint: The folder must exist. A share that is not connected is reported, never replaced by an empty folder.
sync.host_key_confirm: First connection to this server. Check that its key is {{key}}, then trust it.
sync.git_hint: Uses the git command with your own SSH keys or credential helper. Use an empty repository or a branch of its own: each sync replaces the branch with a single commit.
sync.kind_s3: S3 bucket (Amazon S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, R2...)
sync.s3_hint: Works with Amazon S3 and S3-compatible stores. The endpoint is the server's address, such as s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com, s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com, http://localhost:9000 (MinIO on this computer). The region is taken from the endpoint when it names one. The keys need to read and write a single object, reach-vault.reach, in the folder. The file is encrypted before it leaves this device.
sync.probe_empty: Reachable and empty: your data will be written there on the first sync.
sync.probe_this: Reachable, and it holds your vault: this device will join it.
sync.probe_other: This location holds another vault. Choose an empty folder or repository.
sync.backend_note: Choosing a location here moves your personal data there. Other devices follow once you choose the same location on them.
sync.smb_hint: Reach connects to the share itself, so it does not need to be mounted or mapped to a drive letter. The folder must exist.

tmux.name_invalid: The tmux session name can only use letters, digits, - and _ (at most 64 characters).

tmux.kill_failed: Could not end the tmux session: {{error}}
tmux.quit_note: {{count}} of them run in tmux, which keeps running on the server: connect again to get back to it.
tmux.auto_reconnecting: Still running in tmux. Reconnecting by itself.

tmux.pick_detail: Pick a tmux session to attach to, or start a new one.
tmux.pick_none: No tmux sessions are running on this server. Start a new one, or open a normal shell.

settings.term_osc52_desc: Programs on the server (tmux copy mode, vim) can put text on this computer's clipboard with OSC 52. They can never read it.
cursor.style_desc: How the terminal cursor looks. Its color comes from the terminal theme. A session can choose its own, and programs such as vim can still change it while they run.
cursor.blink_desc: The cursor blinks. A session can choose otherwise.
cursor.width_desc: How wide the bar cursor is drawn.
cursor.inactive_desc: How the cursor looks in a terminal that does not have the keyboard: the other pane of a split, or when the window is in the background.
highlight.setting_desc: Shows error and warning words, IP addresses and MAC addresses in the server's output in colour. Only the screen changes: copies, searches and logs keep the text as sent. Full-screen programs such as vim are left alone.
highlight.kinds_desc: Pick what is shown in colour. The colours come from the terminal theme.
highlight.custom_desc: Your own regular expressions, one per line. Plain text matches as written; use /pattern/i to ignore case. Put a colour first to choose it, e.g. #ff8800 \bCRC\b. Lines starting with // are ignored. Your patterns win over the built-in ones.
termbar.label: Terminal bar
termbar.setting_desc: A bar over each terminal with its connection and quick actions: find, files, snippets, history, broadcast, split.
termbar.hover: When the pointer is over the terminal
termbar.logging: Writing this session to a log file
settings.scrollback_desc: Lines a terminal keeps above its screen. Unlimited keeps up to 250,000 lines (50,000 on a phone or tablet); a full terminal uses about 1.5 MB per 1,000 lines.
settings.line_numbers_desc: Numbers each line in a column left of the terminal, counting from the start of the session. A wrapped line keeps one number.
settings.timestamps_desc: Shows when each line was written, in the same column.
phonekeys.title: Extra keys
phonekeys.desc: The keys on the bar above the keyboard. Tap a key on the bar to move it or take it off; tap one below to add it at the end.
phonekeys.show_desc: With a hardware keyboard (Samsung DeX, Bluetooth, USB) the bar is not needed: Automatic hides it while one is attached.
tmux.window_new_tab: New tmux window in new tab
tmux.no_windows: This tmux session has no windows yet.
tmux.bar_hint_window: tmux session {{name}}, window {{window}}: click to switch
settings.tmux_new_tab: New tab opens a tmux window
settings.tmux_new_tab_desc: On a tmux tab, Ctrl+Shift+T and the + button open a new tmux window in a new tab. Off: a local terminal, as on other tabs.
settings.tmux_connect_windows_desc: Connecting to a tmux session opens the window used last, or every window in a tab of its own.
settings.tmux_hide_status_desc: In tmux tabs only, where the tab shows the window's name. Applies to tabs opened from now on.
bulk.key_needed: Pick an imported key or a key file.
bulk.auth_password_hint: Sessions switched to a password take the Password above; left empty, they ask when you connect.
bulk.addresses_only: Only sessions with more than one address.
bulk.os_auto_hint: SSH sessions find their icon again on the next connect; the others get none.
bulk.wol_hint: Applies to {{count}} of {{total}}: sessions with a MAC address. Each keeps its own MAC.
shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.desc: Click a key to change it, + to add another, × to remove one. Escape cancels while you record.
shortcuts.needs_modifier: {{key}} would stop that key reaching the terminal. Add Ctrl or Alt (⌘ on a Mac), or use a function key.
shortcuts.shared_warning: Some keys are on more than one action, so only the first runs: {{list}}
shortcuts.ai_panel: Show or hide the AI panel
shortcuts.broadcast: Add to or remove from the broadcast
files.title: Files: this computer and server
files.move_confirm: Move {{what}} to {{to}}? It is removed from here once copied.
files.overwrite_confirm: {{count}} of them already exist in {{to}} and will be overwritten.
files.delete_confirm: Delete {{what}} on {{where}}? This cannot be undone.
files.keys_hint: Tab switches side · Insert or Space marks · type to jump · {{key}} terminal
files.edit_opened: Opened {{name}}; each save is uploaded to the server
files.edit_upload_failed: Uploading {{name}} failed: {{error}}. Save again to retry.
files.folders_differ: Marked the differences: {{left}} on this computer, {{right}} on the server
files.compare_need_files: Put the cursor on a file on each side to compare them
settings.file_editor_desc: What Edit (F4) in the full-pane file manager opens files in. Terminal editors open in a new terminal tab. A server file is uploaded back each time you save it.
settings.file_editor_command_desc: The program and its options; the file is added at the end. Use quotes around a path with spaces.
settings.file_editor_terminal_desc: Open it in a new terminal tab, for editors such as vim or nano.
session.connect_with_hint: Connects once with this saved credential. The session keeps its own login.
session.connect_to_hint: Pick another address or saved credential for one connect. The session keeps its own.
session.connect_with_ref: Uses a password manager entry, which is approved per session. Link it to the session in the editor to connect with it.
session.connect_with_route: The session's jump hosts or proxy use password manager entries, approved for its own user name, so this credential's other user name cannot be used here.
session.addresses_hint: Other addresses of the same server, such as an office and an internet address, or IPv4 and IPv6. Tried in this order.
session.address_direct_hint: Connect straight, without the jump hosts or proxy
session.connect_mode_auto_hint: Uses the first address in this order that can be reached; if one cannot be reached, the next one is tried.
session.connect_mode_ask_hint: Shows the addresses, and which of them answer, each time you connect.
session.connect_mode_main_hint: Always the main address. Right-click › Connect via still picks another one.
settings.check_addresses_desc: Before connecting a session that has several addresses, check which of them answer from here, to pick the best one. Off (silent mode): nothing is sent to an address until it is tried, and they are tried in order. A session can choose for itself in its settings.
session.address_check_hint: Silent: nothing is sent to an address until it is tried. Automatic then tries them in order and moves on when one cannot be reached.
spice.password_hint: The display's SPICE password, if it has one. For Proxmox VE, use Open SPICE file with the file from the SPICE console button instead.
spice.tls_port_hint: With a TLS port, everything goes encrypted to it and the port above is not used.
spice.ca_hint: The certificate (PEM) of the CA that signed the server's. It is then the only one trusted, and the server's name need not match. Empty: the usual public CAs, and the name must match.
spice.host_subject_hint: Optional: the subject the server's certificate must have, as virt-viewer's host-subject.
spice.via_hint: SPICE without TLS is not encrypted. Through a saved SSH session it is, and the port can stay closed to the network; the host above is then as that SSH server sees it, such as localhost.
password_history.title: Previous passwords ({{count}})
password_history.hint: Use puts the password back in the field above; it is kept when you save, and the current one moves into this list.
password_history.limit_desc: How many previous passwords each session and saved credential keeps, encrypted in its vault and synced with it.
password_history.clear_all_desc: Forget the previous passwords of every session and saved credential, shared vaults included.
password_history.clear_all_confirm: Forget every previous password? Members of shared vaults lose them too.
web.login_auto: Automatic (known devices, then any login form)
web.login_hint: The user name and password are typed into the page's login form, only on this session's own address, and the login button is pressed once per window.
web.login_off_hint: The page opens without signing in.
web.open_window_hint: A separate window that cannot reach the app or other sessions.
web.open_browser_hint: Opens in your browser, which handles certificates itself. Nothing is signed in for you.
web.storage_session_hint: No other session sees this session's cookies.
web.storage_profile_hint: Sessions with the same profile name share cookies, for example the nodes of one cluster.
web.certs_none: None. A self-signed certificate is asked about the first time it is met.
web.certs_hint: Only certificates your system does not trust are checked against this list. Paste a SHA-256 fingerprint to trust one before opening.
web.cert_body: {{host}} ({{session}}) presented a certificate your system does not trust. Check its fingerprint against the device before trusting it.
web.cert_changed: This session trusted a different certificate before. If the device's certificate was not replaced, someone may be between you and it.
x11desktop.label: X11 desktop
x11desktop.hint: Starts a whole desktop on the server and shows it in a window of its own. The server needs X11Forwarding yes and xauth. This computer needs Xephyr (Linux), the X11 server from Settings (Windows) or XQuartz (macOS).
x11desktop.command_needed: Enter the command that starts the desktop.
session.address_via_missing: The SSH session it went through no longer exists
session.address_via_refs: {{name}} logs in with a password manager entry, which is not used when another session goes through it. Save the password in {{name}}, or use a key or the agent.
files.storage_access_hint: To see all of this device's files, not only the app's own folder, allow access to all files.
ftp.password_wrong: The server did not take that password.
ftp.cert_untrusted: The server's certificate is not one this computer trusts (self-signed, expired or for another name). Its SHA-256 fingerprint:
ftp.cert_hint: Trust it only if it is the server's own. It is then kept with the session, which asks again if the certificate changes.
ftp.cert_refused: Not connected: the certificate was not trusted.
ftp.login_hint: Leave the user name empty for an anonymous login. Without a saved password it is asked for on connect.
ftp.tls_implicit: FTPS, implicit (TLS from the start, port 990)
ftp.tls_hint: The login and files go encrypted. A certificate the system does not trust is asked about once and then kept.
ftp.tls_none_hint: The password and files go unencrypted: anyone on the way can read them.
files.keys_hint_files: Tab switches side · Insert or Space marks · type to jump
web.popups_hint: Lets the page open windows of its own, such as an iDRAC or iLO virtual console. They open as more windows of this session, with its cookies and trusted certificates.
net.routed_hint: This address goes through a jump host or proxy; the tools reach it straight from this device.
net.no_host: Type a host name or IP address first.
net.method_hint: Auto sends ICMP echo, and a TCP connect to the port where this device does not allow ICMP.
net.tcp_fallback: This device does not let apps send ICMP, so these are TCP connects to the port. A refused connection still counts as an answer.
net.broadcast_hint: Empty: 255.255.255.255, this network. For a machine on another subnet, use that subnet's broadcast address (10.0.0.255) and let the router forward it.
session.wol_hint: Adds Wake to the session's menu. The machine's network card must have Wake-on-LAN switched on.
servers.intro: Share a folder of this computer with devices on your network.
servers.tftp_desc: For switches, routers and IP phones that load firmware or configs over TFTP.
servers.ftp_desc: Plain FTP, for cameras, printers and older devices.
servers.sftp_desc: Encrypted file transfer over SSH, for any SFTP client.
servers.http_desc: Browse and download from any web browser; uploads too, when allowed.
servers.port_in_use: Port {{port}} is in use by another program.
servers.port_privileged: Port {{port}} needs administrator rights on this computer.
servers.port_no_address: This address no longer belongs to this computer.
servers.no_users: Add a user or allow anonymous access.
servers.tftp_no_login: TFTP has no logins: anyone who can reach it can read the folder.
servers.warn_plain: {{name}} sends passwords and files unencrypted. Use it on networks you trust.
servers.warn_all: Listening on all networks: every network this computer is on can reach it, public Wi-Fi too.
servers.warn_public: {{ip}} is a public address: the internet may reach this server.
capture.unavailable: Nothing to take a picture of yet.
wireguard.missing_error: This session's WireGuard profile no longer exists. Pick another in the session editor.
wireguard.confirm_up: Turn on the WireGuard tunnel “{{name}}” to connect? It reaches {{endpoint}}. Only this app's own connections go through it.
wireguard.declined: Not connected: the WireGuard tunnel “{{name}}” was left off.
wireguard.session_route_hint: The connection goes through this tunnel. If the tunnel is off, connecting asks to turn it on. Nothing changes on the device: only this app's connections use it.
wireguard.session_route_jump_hint: The tunnel carries the connection to the first jump host. If the tunnel is off, connecting asks to turn it on.
wireguard.name: Name
wireguard.conf_hint: Paste the file your WireGuard server or app exported, or import it. It is stored encrypted in the vault, private key included. One [Peer] per profile.
wireguard.new_key_toast: New key pair made. Give the server this public key: {{key}}
wireguard.delete_confirm: Delete the WireGuard profile “{{name}}”? Sessions that use it will not connect until another one is picked.
wireguard.empty: No profiles yet. Add one to send sessions through a WireGuard tunnel.
sync_account.title: Account
sync_account.personal_vault_desc: Sync your encrypted personal vault through this server.
sync_account.sign_in_help: Your browser opens so you can approve this device.
sync_account.managed_removal_desc: Vault owners can request deletion of a revoked shared vault on this device, including unsynced edits.
sync_account.browser_pending: Approve this installation in your browser.
sync_account.signed_out_locally: Signed out on this device. Remove it in the web portal to revoke server access.
sync_account.error_server: Could not complete the request to the sync server.
sync_account.error_revoked: This installation needs to sign in again.
sync_account.error_keychain: Could not access the system credential store.
sync_account.error_callback: Could not receive the browser response.
sync_account.error_url: Enter a server origin using HTTPS. HTTP is allowed for localhost.
sync_account.busy: An account action is already in progress.
sync_account.error_existing: Sign out before connecting another account.
sync_account.error_browser: Could not open the system browser.
sync_account.error_expired: The sign-in request expired. Try again.
sync_account.error_label: Enter a device name of up to 64 characters.
sync_account.sync_preferences_desc: Choose what this installation shares with your account when preference sync is on.
sync_account.preference_server_update: Update the sync server to sync all the preferences selected here.
sync_account.vault_enable: Use this server for vault sync
sync_account.vault_enabled: Encrypted personal vault sync is enabled.
sync_account.vault_confirm: Move personal vault sync to this server? The existing local files and previous sync location are kept.
titlebar.wireguard_on: WireGuard on: {{names}}. Click to see the tunnels.
wireguard.auto_off: Turns off when no session uses it
organization.empty: Create or join an organization in the web portal.
organization.label: Organization
organization.verify_owner_help: Get the vault owner’s public key directly from them through a trusted channel.
organization.verify_owner_required: Verify the vault owner’s public key to resume sync. Your local changes are kept.
organization.rotation_upgrade_required: This key change needs an authenticated rotation. Ask the vault owner to update Reacher CM and rotate the key again.
organization.rotation_update_clients: Update Reacher CM on all devices that use this vault before rotating its key.
organization.transfer_confirm: Transfer ownership? The new owner will manage access and you will lose server access.
organization.no_vaults: You have no vaults in this organization.
bmc.badge_hint: Server management over Redfish (iDRAC, iLO, XCC...)
bmc.editor_hint: Shows the health, sensors, hardware, logs and jobs of a server's management controller (Dell iDRAC, HPE iLO, Supermicro, Lenovo XCC, OpenBMC) over Redfish, and runs power, boot once and virtual media tasks. Enter the controller's address, not the server's.
bmc.connecting: Logging in to the management controller…
bmc.cert_untrusted: This computer does not trust the controller's certificate. That is normal for the self-signed certificate of an iDRAC or iLO. Its SHA-256 fingerprint:
bmc.cert_hint: Compare it with the one in the controller's web interface. Once trusted, it is remembered for this session.
bmc.logs_clear_confirm: Clear {{name}} on {{server}}? Its entries are deleted on the controller and cannot be brought back.
bmc.power_none: This server has no power control here.
bmc.power_harsh: This cuts the server off like pulling its plug: work that is not saved on it is lost.
bmc.boot_hint: Only the next start boots from here; after that the server keeps its usual boot order. Restart it to boot now.
bmc.identify_hint: Lights the server's identify LED, so it can be found in the rack.
bmc.media_none: This controller offers no virtual media.
bmc.media_hint: An http(s), NFS or CIFS address of an image the controller itself can reach. Some controllers need a licence for this (iDRAC Enterprise, iLO Advanced).
bmc.reset_hint: Restarts the iDRAC or iLO itself; the server keeps running. The controller cannot be reached for a few minutes.
bmc.reset_confirm: Restart the management controller of {{server}}? The server keeps running.
bmc.reset_done: The controller is restarting. Try again in a few minutes.
bmc.licence_needed: The controller needs a licence for this. It said: {{message}}
organization.rotation_pending: Uploads are paused until the vault owner rotates the key.
bmc.vnc_tip: The iDRAC's own VNC server in a VNC tab (turn it on under iDRAC Settings › Services › VNC Server).
bmc.vnc_intro: Opens the iDRAC's built-in VNC server, which shows the server's screen like the virtual console.
bmc.vnc_hint: The VNC server must be enabled in the iDRAC (Settings › Services › VNC Server) with its own password (up to 8 characters). Tick SSL encryption when it is on in the iDRAC (any setting but Off); the iDRAC's certificate is then checked like the server management tab's, so trust it there first.
bmc.editor_vnc_hint: For the VNC button and the session menu's Open VNC. With a password saved, VNC opens without asking.
bmc.vnc_refused: The iDRAC refused the VNC password. Type the current one.
bmc.vnc_save: Save the password in the session
bmc.logout_tip: Log out of the controller now, freeing one of its few session slots. The tab stays open.
bmc.remote_console_tip: An iDRAC 9 opens its HTML5 console straight away. Older iDRACs (7, 8) and other controllers open their web interface, signed in: start the console there (on an iDRAC, Dashboard › Virtual Console › Launch).
bmc.ssh_tip: SSH to the controller's own command line (racadm on an iDRAC, SMASH CLP on an iLO), as the same user.
bmc.text_console_intro: Opens an SSH tab to the controller and types its serial console command, so you see the server's text console (BIOS, boot, a Linux serial login). It logs in as this session does.
bmc.console_command_none: None: the login opens the console
bmc.console_command_hint: Filled in for this controller: console com2 on an iDRAC, vsp on an iLO, console 1 on an XCC. Leave empty for a controller whose SSH opens the console itself (OpenBMC on port 2200).
proxmox.badge_hint: Proxmox session: nodes, guests, tasks and consoles
proxmox.realm_hint: Used when the user name has no @realm. A name like admin@pve keeps its own.
proxmox.editor_hint: Shows a Proxmox VE node or cluster: nodes, guests, storage and tasks, with power actions, snapshots and consoles (SPICE, display, text). Port 8006 is Proxmox VE, 8007 a Backup Server. With an API token the pages need no password, but Proxmox opens consoles only for a user login, so the password (and code) is asked for when a console opens.
proxmox.code_hint: A code from your authenticator app, or a recovery key.
proxmox.code_refused: That code was not accepted. Try the next one.
proxmox.cert_untrusted: This server's certificate is not signed by anyone this computer trusts; Proxmox makes its own at install. Check that the fingerprint matches the one under the node's Certificates:
proxmox.cert_hint: Once trusted, it is remembered for this session. A different certificate is asked about again.
proxmox.token_hint: The pages use the API token of {{user}}. Consoles ask for the user's password the first time.
proxmox.filter: Filter by name, ID, node or tag
proxmox.console_login_intro: Proxmox opens consoles only for a user login, not an API token. Log in as this session's user; the login is kept while the tab is open.
proxmox.console_login_needed: This console needs a user login.
proxmox.node_reboot_intro: Reboot {{node}}? Its running guests are shut down first and start again as set to start at boot.
proxmox.node_shutdown_intro: Shut down {{node}}? Its guests stop with it, and it stays off until someone turns it on.
proxmox.spice_hint: SPICE is offered when the VM's display is SPICE (qxl).
proxmox.snap_name_hint: Start with a letter, then letters, digits, - and _ (up to 40).
proxmox.snap_with_ram: Include RAM (the VM resumes where it was)
proxmox.confirm_stop: Stop {{guest}} now? Like pulling its plug: anything unsaved is lost.
proxmox.confirm_reset: Reset {{guest}} now? Like pressing its reset button: anything unsaved is lost.
proxmox.confirm_rollback: Roll {{guest}} back to {{snapshot}}? Everything since that snapshot is lost.
proxmox.pbs_filter: Filter by ID, owner or comment
proxmox.pbs_protected_hint: Pruning and forgetting leave it alone.
proxmox.pbs_confirm_forget: Forget the backup {{snapshot}} on {{store}}? Its data is gone after the next garbage collection.
sync_account.pair_help: In the sync web portal, open Devices → Add device → Pair a phone or tablet.
sync_account.pair_match: Compare this code in the web portal, then approve the device there.
sync_account.pair_invalid: Enter a Reacher CM mobile pairing code.
sync_account.pair_camera: Camera access is required to scan. You can paste the pairing code instead.
sync_account.mobile_vault_link_help: On a trusted device with personal vault sync enabled, open Settings > Sync and show its link code under This device. Scan it or paste it on this device.
sync_account.vault_link_confirm: This device will open the linked personal vault. Its previous local vault will stay on this device and can be restored in Settings > Backup.
sync_account.local_vault_restore_confirm: Open your previous local vault again? The linked vault stays on disk and on the sync server. You may need the previous password.
sync.account_sign_in_first: Sign in to your sync server under Connection at the top of this page first.
sync.turso_personal_elsewhere: Your personal data syncs to another location now.
sync.turso_shared_vaults_desc: These stay on Turso whichever location your personal data uses.
sync.turso_shared_none: No shared vaults on Turso yet.
sync.export_backup_key_desc: The key that opens your vaults on this device. Keep a copy in case the system keychain is lost.
sync.local_vault_restore_desc: The local vault this device used before it was linked or moved to a sync server.
